doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

title: Why the orchestration is in E rather than E flat
summary: Broadbent describes E as bright, full and warm for strings, versus a darker E flat.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah. Do you purposely, you mentioned that you orchestrated it for the orchestra in the key of E. Does E have a different sound than E flat?

Oh yeah. Oh absolutely. E flat would be a darker sound, especially when there are strings involved, a lot of strings, and we had a lot. E becomes a bright, full, open stringed sound, but warm. E flat they’ve got a lot of stops on the — how’s that for a piano player, folks?
Anyway you know what I mean?
